rationale: A 30-year-old female presented with a 2-year history of intermittent hemoptysis, dyspnea, and a right hilar soft tissue mass encasing the pulmonary artery. evidence_items.source_quote: Serological studies for histoplasmosis, Aspergillus and connective tissue disease were negative.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum Cryptococcus neoformans and histoplasmosis antigens were negative.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum cryptococcal, urine Histoplasma, and Blastomyces antigen tests were obtained and were negative.

rationale: A 25-year-old female presented with migratory polyarthralgia, purpuric rash, weight loss, microscopic hematuria, and hemoptysis with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. rationale: A 34-year-old pregnant female at 31 weeks gestation presented with high fever, headache, macular rash, elevated liver enzymes, and impending respiratory failure. rationale: A 15-year-old male presenting with fever, cough, altered mental status, multiple ring-enhancing brain abscesses, and an esophagopleural fistula. evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnostic workup was negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, toxoplasmosis, neurocysticercosis, HIV, histoplasmosis, cryptococcosis, blastomycosis, and free-living amoebas.

rationale: A 32-year-old male with HIV presenting with painful scattered purplish cutaneous nodules, cough, and pleural effusions. rationale: A 52-year-old male with systemic lupus erythematosus on long-term immunosuppression presenting with fever, cough, renal failure, cytopenias, and fungal septicemia. Initial bone marrow smear revealed yeast-like fungi raising suspicion for Histoplasma capsulatum. However, metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and subsequent pure fungal culture with Sanger sequencing definitively identified the pathogen as Emergomyces orientalis (disseminated emergomycosis). Preliminary suspicion of histoplasmosis was refuted and ruled out by definitive molecular identification of Emergomyces orientalis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: On the sixth day of hospitalization, a bone marrow smear revealed hemophagocytic cells and yeast-like fungi, raising suspicions of Histoplasma capsulatus infection. Therefore, a repeat bone marrow puncture and mNGS were performed to identify the pathogen. Initial cultures of bone marrow and blood remained negative. Following the bone marrow smear results, the samples were removed from the blood culture system, centrifuged, and the precipitates inoculated on Sabouraud agar, cultured at both 28 C and 35 C. By the tenth day of admission, the mNGS report confirmed Emergomyces orientalis infection.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial bone marrow cytology suspected Histoplasma capsulatum, but mNGS and culture sequencing definitively proved Emergomyces orientalis; resolved as false-positive morphological suspicion refuted by molecular diagnostics.

rationale: A 67-year-old male liver transplant recipient presenting with sudden and progressive hoarseness, diagnosed with laryngeal cryptococcosis via vocal cord biopsy. rationale: A 67-year-old female with cirrhosis presenting with fever, altered mental status, and miliary pulmonary nodules, ultimately diagnosed with disseminated tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis. rationale: A 26-year-old female presented with scotoma and multiple fundic white dots, diagnosed with multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS). Diagnostic evaluation included blood tests and medical history to investigate differential infectious and inflammatory diagnoses including ocular histoplasmosis syndrome, all of which were ruled out. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: However, a complete medical history was taken, and a blood test was requested to perform a differential diagnosis with systemic and ocular infectious entities such as syphilis, diffuse unilateral subacute neuroretinitis, and ocular histoplasmosis syndrome, as well as noninfectious entities such as sarcoidosis, sympathetic ophthalmia, Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome, and intraocular lymphoma, that were ruled out.

rationale: A 49-year-old male with HIV/AIDS presented with acute respiratory distress and an obstructing left mainstem bronchial mass diagnosed as HSV-1/2 endobronchial pseudotumor. Infectious evaluation on bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) included fungal antigen studies for histoplasmosis, which were negative. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was performed and sent for gram stain, aerobic and anaerobic cultures, viral cultures, acid fast bacilli (AFB), pneumocystis DNA PCR, fungal antigen studies including histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, and aspergillus, and cytology. The aerobic and anaerobic culture was positive for group B streptococcus but all other tests were negative.

rationale: A 27-year-old female evaluated for bilateral sacroiliac disease and panuveitis prior to initiating TNF inhibitor therapy. Pre-treatment infectious workup included diagnostic testing for endemic fungal infections (Histoplasmosis, Blastomycosis, and Coccidioides), which was explicitly negative. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

Infectious evaluation included serum histoplasmosis antibodies and urine histoplasmosis antigen, both of which were negative. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum histoplasmosis antibodies, urine histoplasmosis antigen, serum coccidioidomycosis antibodies, and a rapid respiratory pathogen panel were negative.

rationale: A 26-year-old male with advanced untreated HIV presenting with hemoptysis, fever, and diffuse pulmonary nodules, diagnosed with disseminated Kaposi Sarcoma and Kaposi Sarcoma inflammatory cytokine syndrome (KICS). Extensive infectious workup included urine Histoplasma antigen, which was negative. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Additional fungal testing was also negative, including serum beta-D-glucan and galactomannan, serum cryptococcal antigen, urine histoplasma antigen, serum blastomycoses antigen, and sputum fungal cultures.

rationale: A 28-year-old male with newly diagnosed advanced HIV (CD4 14 cells/uL) presenting with fever, severe acute respiratory failure, and ARDS requiring VV ECMO. As part of an extensive infectious workup for opportunistic pulmonary and systemic infections, fungal infections including disseminated histoplasmosis were explicitly excluded based on negative fungal cultures. Giemsa staining and PCR of BAL and bone marrow confirmed disseminated toxoplasmosis. Histoplasmosis was investigated in the differential diagnosis and ruled out by negative fungal cultures -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Other fungal infections, including disseminated histoplasmosis, were excluded based on negative fungal cultures.

rationale: A 43-year-old female from Venezuela presenting with a large, chronic, painful ulcerated wound on her lower left shin. Extensive infectious disease diagnostic workup was performed, and testing for Histoplasma, galactomannan, Fungitell, Blastomyces, and Coccidioides was explicitly negative. The CDC PCR of an excised lesion confirmed cutaneous leishmaniasis (Leishmania panamensis). Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

rationale: A male patient with advanced AIDS, pulmonary abnormalities, and pancytopenia. Targeted diagnostic evaluation for Histoplasma was performed, and both a urinary antigen test and bone marrow PCR for Histoplasma were explicitly negative. Although the infectious disease team empirically initiated itraconazole due to continued suspicion, specific microbiological and molecular testing for Histoplasma capsulatum refuted the diagnosis, and the patient was ultimately diagnosed with disseminated nocardiosis and lymphoma. Target disease was explicitly tested and negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A urinary antigen test for Histoplasma, performed on January 30, 2024, was negative.
Polymerase chain reaction for Histoplasma and mycobacteria on the BM sample was negative.

step10_contradiction_notes: The infectious disease team empirically initiated itraconazole based on persistent clinical suspicion, but specific urinary antigen and bone marrow PCR for Histoplasma were explicitly negative.

rationale: A 35-year-old female presenting with cholestatic liver injury, severe hypercholesterolemia, and non-caseating epithelioid granulomas on liver biopsy. Comprehensive etiological evaluation of the hepatic granulomas included diagnostic testing for histoplasmosis, tuberculosis, syphilis, toxoplasmosis, rubella, leptospirosis, Q fever, Schistosoma, brucella, and leishmaniasis, all of which were negative. Histochemical fungal stains (PAS and Grocott) showed no microorganisms. The patient was diagnosed with hepatic and pulmonary sarcoidosis. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Mycobacterium tuberculosis work-up was negative, and the hepatic granuloma etiological study was negative for syphilis, toxoplasmosis, rubella, leptospirosis, Q fever, Schistosoma, brucella, leishmaniasis and histoplasmosis.
evidence_items.test_name: Hepatic granuloma etiological workup / Histoplasmosis diagnostic testing

rationale: A 9-year-old male presenting with recurrent bone pain and lytic lesions of the femur and tibia. As part of an extensive infectious evaluation for osteolytic bone lesions, Histoplasma urine antigen, Blastomyces antibody, Lyme serology, hepatitis, and HIV tests were performed and were all explicitly negative. Subsequent bone biopsy confirmed Gaucher disease with low beta-glucosidase enzyme activity. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Workup for infectious causes included Lyme antibody testing, HIV antigen and antibody screen, hepatitis B panel, hepatitis C polymerase chain reaction (PCR), Quantiferon, Histoplasma urine antigen, and Blastomyces antibody, which were all negative.

rationale: A 37-year-old male with severe COVID-19 acute respiratory failure requiring VV ECMO. An extensive diagnostic workup including diagnostic bronchoscopy was performed specifically to rule out histoplasmosis, aspergillosis, blastomycosis, malignancy, and sarcoidosis. Histopathological examination of bronchoscopic samples demonstrated non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP), diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and pulmonary hypertension without fungal organisms, ruling out histoplasmosis. Target disease investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: An extensive workup, including diagnostic bronchoscopy, was performed to rule out conditions such as aspergillosis, blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, malignancy, and sarcoidosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Bronchoscopic findings revealed histological features (Figure 2) consistent with non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP), diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and pulmonary hypertension.

rationale: A 52-year-old female presenting with severe COVID-19 pneumonia and extensive bilateral lung involvement. Diagnostic infectious serology was performed to evaluate for endemic fungal infections and coinfections; serological tests for histoplasmosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, HIV, and initial aspergillosis were explicitly negative. Bronchial washings subsequently grew Aspergillus welwitschiae. Histoplasmosis was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Renal and liver function tests were normal, and serological tests for HIV, paracoccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis, and aspergillosis were negative.

rationale: A 54-year-old male presented with a two-year history of bloody diarrhea, fever, abdominal pain, and bowel perforation. Diagnostic evaluation for infectious etiologies of pyrexia of unknown origin and ulcerative intestinal lesions was performed; active tuberculosis was excluded by GeneXpert, viral serologies for HIV and syphilis were negative, and clinical examination noted no cutaneous markers of disseminated histoplasmosis. Histopathological and immunohistochemical analysis of surgical colectomy specimens confirmed primary intestinal NK/T-cell lymphoma. Target disease was evaluated in the patient workup and absent/ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: There were no cutaneous markers of disseminated histoplasmosis.

rationale: A 59-year-old female with a history of invasive lobular breast carcinoma presented with nausea, vomiting, headache, and altered mental status. Diagnostic evaluation including lumbar puncture revealed low CSF glucose, elevated protein, and monocyte-predominant leukocytosis with malignant adenocarcinoma cells. Because of low CSF glucose and fever, an infectious disease workup was undertaken including bacterial, atypical, and fungal etiologies (tuberculosis, West Nile, Cryptococcus, and histoplasma), which was explicitly negative. The patient was diagnosed with leptomeningeal carcinomatosis and myelophthisic anemia from metastatic breast cancer. Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Her labs showed leukocytosis with a negative infectious disease workup, which included bacterial and atypical/fungal infections (tuberculosis, West Nile, Cryptococcus, and histoplasma) due to the finding of low CSF glucose.

rationale: A 26-year-old male with a history of treated Hodgkin lymphoma and outdoor exposures (spelunking and rafting) presented with fever, cervical mass, and cavitary pulmonary solid nodules with ground-glass opacities. Diagnostic infectious evaluation was performed; an extensive workup explicitly excluded histoplasmosis, pulmonary aspergillosis, tuberculosis, bacterial endocarditis, and systemic embolism. Serial blood cultures and bronchoalveolar lavage were unremarkable, and PAS and Grocott staining of lung biopsy showed no fungal structures. Cervical node biopsy confirmed relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma, and lung biopsy confirmed synchronous primary pulmonary extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (ENKTL). Target disease was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Extensive workup excluded bacterial endocarditis, tuberculosis, systemic embolism, pulmonary aspergillosis, and histoplasmosis.
Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Grocott staining showed no fungal structures.

rationale: A 65-year-old female presenting with subacute thoracic back pain, hypercalcemia, and diffuse osteolytic bone lesions on whole-body CT. As part of an extensive infectious and malignant workup, comprehensive fungal serologies including Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Cryptococcus, and Coccidioides were negative. Histopathologic examination of an elbow nodule confirmed a necrobiotic granuloma negative for microorganisms on GMS/PASD stains, establishing a diagnosis of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. Histoplasmosis was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Comprehensive fungal serologies including Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Cryptococcus, and Coccidioides were negative.

rationale: A 59-year-old male presenting with acute-on-chronic lower back pain, bilateral radiculopathy, and widespread osteolytic lesions with bone hypermetabolism on PET-CT. Infectious diagnostic testing was conducted to evaluate for fungal osteomyelitis, and cryptococcus, blastomycoses, histoplasma, and coccidioides antigens were not detected. Bone biopsies confirmed necrotizing granulomas negative for malignancy or infection, establishing osseous sarcoidosis. Histoplasmosis was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cryptococcus, blastomycoses, histoplasma, and Coccidioides antigens were not detected.
evidence_items.test_name: Fungal antigen panel including Histoplasma antigen

rationale: A 41-year-old male presenting with subacute inflammatory monoarthritis of the left knee and cutaneous nodules following river camping. Initial fungal antigen tests returned positive for Histoplasma antigen in urine (5.20 ng/mL), serum (1.03 ng/mL), and synovial fluid (1.76 ng/mL). However, skin biopsies demonstrated broad-based budding yeasts on GMS/PAS stains, and culture with MALDI-TOF MS definitively identified Blastomyces dermatitidis/gilchristii. Clinicians interpreted the positive Histoplasma antigen results as false positives resulting from known cross-reactivity with Blastomyces. Histoplasmosis was ruled out and blastomycosis was confirmed -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The positive Histoplasma antigens detected in urine, serum, and synovial fluid were interpreted as false positives due to well-described antigenic cross-reactivity with Blastomyces dermatitidis, given histopathologic and culture confirmation of blastomycosis.

evidence_items.specimen: urine, serum, synovial fluid, and skin tissue

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial positive Histoplasma antigen across urine, serum, and synovial fluid was contradicted by tissue histopathology and fungal culture identifying Blastomyces dermatitidis; definitively resolved as false-positive cross-reactivity.

rationale: An 89-year-old female with cardiac amyloidosis presenting with chronic ulcerative digital and nasal lesions. Serum Histoplasma antibody immunodiffusion was negative, while quantitative urine Histoplasma antigen was weakly positive at 0.33 ng/mL. Tissue biopsy and fungal culture grew yeast with multiple buds, definitively identified as Paracoccidioides species (P. brasiliensis complex) via ribosomal DNA sequencing and CDC immunodiffusion. The positive urine Histoplasma antigen was attributed to known cross-reactivity with Paracoccidioides, ruling out histoplasmosis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Further testing included negative serum Blastomyces, Histoplasma, and Coccidioides antibody immunodiffusion testing and (1 3)-beta-D-Glucan. Quantitative Histoplasma antigen from the urine was positive at 0.33 ng/mL (reference range >0.20 ng/mL positive). The result report noted cross-reactions occur with Blastomyces spp., Coccidioides spp., and Paracoccidioides brasiliensis.
evidence_items.test_name: Serum Histoplasma antibody immunodiffusion and quantitative urine Histoplasma antigen

step10_contradiction_notes: Weakly positive urine Histoplasma antigen was contradicted by negative serum Histoplasma immunodiffusion and definitive ITS/D1-D2 ribosomal DNA sequencing and CDC immunodiffusion confirming Paracoccidioides brasiliensis complex; resolved as cross-reactivity.

rationale: A 29-year-old male with SLE presenting with fever, neck pain, and septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein (Lemierre's syndrome) after swimming in a pool with a dead pigeon. Comprehensive infectious evaluation specifically included urine Histoplasma galactomannan antigen testing, which was negative (<0.2 ng/mL). Patient improved on anticoagulation, antibiotics, and corticosteroids. Histoplasmosis was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Further infectious workup done with toxoplasma gondii Ab IgM < 3 AUmL (negative < 8.0 AU/mL), HIV-1/2 combo antigen/antibody non-reactive, cryptococcal Ag serum negative, Histoplasma galactomannan Ag Ur negative (reference range < 0.2 ng/mL).

rationale: Patient presenting with persistent fevers undergoing extensive infectious and oncologic evaluation for fever of unknown origin. On hospital days 5-7, diagnostic testing specifically evaluated for Histoplasma along with a panel of other infectious pathogens, and the patient tested negative. Histoplasmosis was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: On days 5-7, the patient tested negative for Histoplasma, Coccidioides, Blastomyces, Brucella, Coxiella, Bartonella, Epstein-Barr virus, and tick panel.

rationale: A 33-year-old male presenting with verrucous facial and occipital scalp plaques. Biopsy next-generation sequencing (NGS) reported 89.17% Blastomyces dermatitidis and 11.46% Histoplasma capsulatum. However, fungal culture and isolate molecular sequencing definitively confirmed Blastomyces dermatitidis, and the patient was diagnosed with primary cutaneous blastomycosis and successfully treated with itraconazole. Histoplasmosis was ruled out and contradicted by isolate sequencing and fungal culture -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis from the biopsy indicated the presence of Blastomyces dermatitidis with a relative abundance of 89.17% and *Histoplasma capsulatum* with a relative abundance of 11.46%.
evidence_items.test_name: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) from scalp plaque biopsy

evidence_items.source_quote: Molecular sequencing confirmed the isolate as Blastomyces dermatitidis. Further questioning revealed that the patient had lived in Ohio and Indiana for 3.5 years, with only incidental exposure to a Golden Retriever and no recollection of trauma or immunosuppressive therapy. On return to China, CT of the thorax was clear and the patient remained afebrile and asymptomatic from a respiratory standpoint. A diagnosis of primary cutaneous blastomycosis was therefore made.
evidence_items.test_name: Isolate molecular sequencing and definitive clinical diagnosis

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial biopsy NGS reported 11.46% relative abundance of Histoplasma capsulatum alongside 89.17% Blastomyces dermatitidis, but subsequent fungal culture and molecular sequencing of the fungal isolate definitively confirmed Blastomyces dermatitidis exclusively, establishing primary cutaneous blastomycosis and ruling out histoplasmosis.
